slides.title: Multi-Step Proportion Problems
slides.note: Post the learning target. Say one line and nothing else yet: “Today: one unit rate, used twice — and two rates put in the same unit before anyone says which is bigger.”

slides.title: Warm-Up
slides.sub: On your own. Four minutes. No notes.
slides.note: Q4 is the unit rate every board today starts from. A room that cannot write 180 for 3 as 60 for 1 cannot use a rate twice. Two minutes silent, then reveal — 43 minutes today, so no discussion on the warm-up.

slides.title: Warm-Up
slides.note: Reveal. Ask for the band each question came from only if time allows.

slides.title: Vocabulary
slides.sub: The new words, before they are used.
slides.note: Read each word and its meaning once; the notes use them next. Students copy the words, not the definitions.

slides.title: Notes
slides.note: A car gets 23 miles per gallon and its tank holds 17.5 gal: 23 × 17.5 = 402.5 mi on a tank. A 1,207-mi trip: 1,207 ÷ 402.5 = 2.998…, so it uses 3 tanks of gas (a part of a tank is still a tank). The rate was used once to find the range and once more to count tanks — two steps, one proportional relationship, and the first answer is not the answer. **Say:** a multi-step problem is the same rate used again; name what each step finds.

slides.title: Notes
slides.note: 100 km/h against 65 mi/h: nothing compares until the units match. 1 km = 0.62 mi, so 100 km/h is 62 mi/h — the second car is faster, though 100 is the bigger number. Convert one rate into the other's unit, then compare. **Say:** which is faster is a question you refuse until both speeds are in the same unit.

slides.title: Notes
slides.note: 12 cookies take 1½ cups of flour. 30 cookies is 30 ÷ 12 = 2.5 times the recipe, so 2.5 × 1½ = 3¾ cups — and a 3-cup bag is not enough. The scale factor is a ratio of the yields, and it multiplies every ingredient; the last step compares to what is on hand. A mixture is the same move: paint 1 : 2 : 3 with 4 gal of the first color has k = 4, and the whole is 6 parts × 4 = 24 gal. **Say:** find k from the yields, multiply the ingredient, then answer the question that was asked.

slides.title: Example 1
slides.note: Ask which unit the comparison will be made in before anyone computes.

slides.title: Example 1
slides.note: A: 8.05 km in ⅔ h is 12.075 km/h; B: 9 km in ¾ h is 12 km/h. A, by a little. A board that compared 5 to 9 compared miles to kilometers.

slides.note: A: 6.44 km in ½ h is 12.88 km/h; B: 7 km in 7⁄12 h is 12 km/h. A is faster.

slides.title: Example 2
slides.note: k = 2.5, so 6¼ cups; 5 cups is 2 recipes, 16 servings. A board with 50 servings scaled the yield by the cups.

slides.note: k = 2, 3 cups; 4½ cups is 3 recipes, 18 servings. A board with 27 servings scaled the yield by the cups.

slides.title: Independent Set
slides.sub: Six questions. On your own, in writing.
slides.note: Hand out the Independent Set; the same six questions are on the board. Silent work. Circulate and mark what you see; do not teach. Whatever is not finished goes home.
